## Background

Today we are going ot learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R. 

There are tons of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the `plot()` function we used last day) and add on packages like **ggplot2**

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

We can use the in-build data frame `cars` to play with plotting:

```{r}
head(cars)
```

```{r}
plot(cars)
```
Now with ggplot: 
First I need to install the package with `install.packages()` 

> I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot2"` in my quarto document as this will result in me re-installing the package every time I render my report. 

Every time I want to use a function from a given package I need to load it up with a `library()` call:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 things: 

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (how the columns of the data map to the plot)
- the **geometry** (how you want the plot drawn: points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) + 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method="lm") +
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x="Speed (mph)",
       y="Stopping distance (ft)",
       title="Silly Plot of Stopping Distances")
```

## Gene Expression Plot

Read the data from online:

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes)+
  aes(x=Condition1,y=Condition2) +
  geom_point()
```

> Q. How many genes are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

> Q. How many are "up" regulated

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```

```{r}
#genes$State == "up"
```

```{r}
sum(genes$State == "up")
```
>Q.What percentage of genes are "down" regulated?

```{r}
down <- sum(genes$State == "down")
total <- nrow(genes)
ans <- round (down/total * 100,4)

```

The percentage of down genes is `r ans`% and that is that...

```{r}
myplot <- ggplot(genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) +
  geom_point() + 
  scale_color_manual (values=c("blue","gray","red")) + 
  labs(x="Control (no drug)", y="Drug Treatment", title="Gene Expression Changes Upon Drug Treatment", subtitle="GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo")
```

```{r}
myplot + 
  theme_bw()
```
We can install extra packages with `install.pacakges()` like theme packages for spongebob colors or actually useful ones like **patchwork** for combining plots: 

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4)
```

```{r}
myplot +
  facet_wrap(~State)
```
## The GapMinder data

The gapminder dataset is quite famous and has lots of stuff we can plot :)  

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

> Q. How many data entries are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many countries are in the dataset?

```{r}
## First look at the table of data
head(gapminder)
```

```{r}
unique(gapminder$country)
```

```{r}
length (unique(gapminder$country))
```

```{r}
ggplot(data=gapminder)+
  aes(gdpPercap,lifeExp) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3)
```

Add some color...

```{r}
ggplot(data=gapminder)+
  aes(gdpPercap,lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point()
```
Separate by continent
```{r}
ggplot(data=gapminder)+
  aes(gdpPercap,lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point()+
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```

Histograms of 
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder)+
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent)+
  geom_histogram()
```

Make a boxplot
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder)+
  aes(lifeExp, continent, fill=continent)+
  geom_boxplot()
```
